user.title: Add memory store
user.description: The name, the embeddings binding and the backend. The last two answers decide what the next step asks for.

data_description.name: Lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter or underscore. This is the name search_memory and smartchain.clear_memory refer to, and for a file-based backend it is also the database filename — renaming a store points it at a fresh, empty one.
data_description.embeddings: Which embeddings binding turns text into vectors for this store. Stores resolve a binding by its title, so a title used twice resolves to nothing at all.
data_description.description: One line telling the model what lives in this store, so it can choose between several. Shown in the search_memory tool description.
data_description.backend_type: Where the vectors are kept. sqlite_numpy needs nothing installed and is the right default; sqlite_vec is faster on large stores; pgvector and qdrant put the vectors on a server you already run.
data_description.source_type: 'none' is a memory store: conversation turns go in, search_memory reads them back. 'entities' turns it into a semantic index of your home for search_entities — the two cannot be combined, because retention would delete the index by age.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure memory store
reconfigure.description: The name, the embeddings binding and the backend. The last two answers decide what the next step asks for.

details.title: Store settings
details.description: The settings that depend on the backend and on what the store holds.

data.path: Database file (leave empty for the default)
data.index_states: Also record each entity's current state
data.include: Always include (a domain, or a full entity id)
data.exclude: Never include (a domain, or a full entity id)

data_description.path: An absolute path to the SQLite file. Leave empty to keep it in Home Assistant's .storage directory, named after the store.
data_description.dsn: postgresql://user:password@host/database. Stored with Home Assistant's other credentials and never shown again — leave empty when editing to keep the one already saved.
data_description.table: Lowercase letters, digits and underscores. It is written straight into SQL and cannot be quoted, which is why the shape is restricted.
data_description.url: https://host:6333 — the base URL of the Qdrant server.
data_description.api_key: Never shown again once saved — leave empty when editing to keep the one already stored. Leave empty on a server that needs no key.
data_description.collection: Lowercase letters, digits and underscores. It becomes part of a URL path and cannot be escaped, which is why the shape is restricted.
data_description.verify_ssl: Turn off only for a server with a self-signed certificate; doing so removes protection against an intercepted connection.
data_description.retention_days: Older memories are deleted once a day. 0 keeps everything forever, which on a busy install grows without limit.
data_description.ingest_conversation: When on, every exchange with an agent is embedded into this store so the agent can recall it later. Turn off for a store you fill yourself.
data_description.preset: How much of the home the index covers, smallest to largest. 'optimal' deliberately leaves out device_tracker: presence data is the most sensitive domain and indexing sends it to the embeddings provider.
data_description.index_states: Records the current state alongside each entity, refreshed periodically. It makes filtering possible; it does not make states searchable by meaning.
data_description.include: Added on top of the preset. Accepts a bare domain (sensor) or a full entity id (sensor.kitchen_temperature).
data_description.exclude: Applied last and wins over both the preset and the include list.

error.invalid_name: A store name must be lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter or underscore.
error.name_taken: Another memory store already uses this name.
error.embeddings_required: Pick which embeddings binding this store uses.
error.embeddings_unknown: No embeddings binding has that name.
error.embeddings_ambiguous: That embeddings title is claimed by more than one binding, so it resolves to nothing. Rename one of them first.
error.dsn_required: The pgvector backend needs a connection string.

user.title: Add tool
user.description: The name, what the tool does, and what happens when the model calls it. The last two answers decide what the next step asks for.

data.name: Tool name
data.action_type: What happens when the model calls it

data_description.name: Lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter or underscore. This is the name the model calls, and the name an agent's “Allowed tools” setting refers to. The six built-in tool names are reserved.
data_description.description: The only thing the model reads when deciding whether to call this tool. Say what it does and when to use it, not how it is implemented.
data_description.enabled: Turn a tool off without deleting it. A disabled tool is not offered to any agent, and does not reserve its name against another tool.
data_description.action_type: service calls a Home Assistant action, template renders Jinja and returns the text, rest calls an HTTP endpoint, script runs a script. Changing this changes which fields the rest of the form asks for.
data_description.params_mode: simple is one row per argument and covers almost every tool. advanced is a raw JSON Schema box, for shapes rows cannot express — anyOf, nested objects, arrays.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure tool
reconfigure.description: The name, what the tool does, and what happens when the model calls it. The last two answers decide what the next step asks for.

data.name: Tool name
data.action_type: What happens when the model calls it

data_description.name: Lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter or underscore. This is the name the model calls, and the name an agent's “Allowed tools” setting refers to. The six built-in tool names are reserved.
data_description.description: The only thing the model reads when deciding whether to call this tool. Say what it does and when to use it, not how it is implemented.
data_description.enabled: Turn a tool off without deleting it. A disabled tool is not offered to any agent, and does not reserve its name against another tool.
data_description.action_type: service calls a Home Assistant action, template renders Jinja and returns the text, rest calls an HTTP endpoint, script runs a script. Changing this changes which fields the rest of the form asks for.

details.title: Tool details
details.description: The arguments the model passes, and the settings of the action type chosen on the previous step.

data.response: Return the action's response to the model

data_description.params_rows: The arguments the model passes when it calls this tool. Reference one inside a template by its bare name: {{ city }}, not {{ args.city }}. Leave the list empty for a tool that takes no arguments.
data_description.params_json: A JSON Schema object describing the call's arguments — an object with "type": "object" and a "properties" map. Validated before it is saved, and again against every call the model makes.
data_description.service: The action to call, e.g. light.turn_on. Picked from the actions registered right now; an action from an integration that is not loaded can still be typed in.
data_description.target: Which entities, devices or areas the action runs on.
data_description.service_data: Extra data passed to the action. Values may contain {{ }} templates referencing the tool's arguments.
data_description.response: On for an action that returns data the model should read (a forecast, a snapshot analysis). Off returns just “OK”. The action must support returning a response.
data_description.value_template: Rendered with the tool's arguments in scope; the rendered text is what the model gets back.
data_description.method: The HTTP method used for the request.
data_description.url: May contain {{ }} templates referencing the tool's arguments.
data_description.headers: Sent with the request; values may template too. Header values are never shown again once saved — leave one blank to keep the stored value, or type a new one to replace it.
data_description.payload: JSON request body, for POST and PUT. Leave empty to send no body at all, which is not the same as sending an empty object.
data_description.timeout: How long to wait for the endpoint, 1–120 seconds.
data_description.response_format: json parses the response and hands the model the parsed data; text hands back the raw body.
data_description.variables: Passed to the script as variables; values may contain {{ }} templates referencing the tool's arguments.

error.invalid_name: A tool name must be lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter or underscore.
error.reserved_name: That name belongs to a built-in tool. A custom tool cannot replace a built-in — pick another name.
error.name_taken: Another tool already uses this name.
error.mcp_name_taken: A connected MCP server already provides a tool with this name. Pick another name, or give that server a prefix in tools.yaml.
error.description_required: Describe what the tool does. This is the only thing the model reads when deciding whether to call it.
error.invalid_parameters_json: The arguments box does not contain valid JSON.
error.invalid_parameters: Arguments must be a JSON Schema object: an object with "type": "object" and a "properties" map.
error.invalid_parameter_name: An argument name must be letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter or underscore.
error.duplicate_parameter: Two arguments have the same name.
error.service_required: Pick the Home Assistant action this tool calls.
error.invalid_service: An action is written as domain.action, e.g. light.turn_on.
error.value_template_required: Write the template this tool renders.
error.url_required: The rest action needs a URL.
error.script_required: Pick the script this tool runs.
error.invalid_script: A script action targets a script.* entity.
error.invalid_action: The action is not valid for its type. The detail is in the Home Assistant log — it is withheld here because an action can carry a credential.
error.unstorable: The value in this field can not be saved. Remove it, or retype it as plain text.

weather_forecast.name: Weather forecast
weather_forecast.description: Will it rain tomorrow afternoon? Assist reports the weather now; this answers questions about later.

sun_times.name: Sun times
sun_times.description: Sunrise, sunset, dawn and dusk, for anything that depends on daylight.

calendar_events.name: Calendar events
calendar_events.description: What is planned. Reads events from a calendar over the range the question is about.

todo_list_items.name: To-do list items
todo_list_items.description: Reads a to-do or shopping list back. Assist can add to a list but cannot tell you what is on it.

area_summary.name: Area summary
area_summary.description: What is on in one room, in a single call, instead of the model guessing entity names one at a time.

who_is_home.name: Who is home
who_is_home.description: Who is home and who is away, without assembling the answer out of entity names.

look_at_camera.name: Look at a camera
look_at_camera.description: Looks at a camera mid-conversation and describes what is visible.

notify_device.name: Notify a device
notify_device.description: Lets the agent reach you: a notification sent to a device or a person, rather than only an answer.
